skill.displayName: 商机雷达-比招标更早发现机会

version.changelog:

- 保留原有渠道归因、账号归属、凭证配置和计费规则。

llm.summary: The skill’s opportunity-search purpose is coherent, but it also performs vendor account setup, stores an API key locally, sends a device-derived identifier, and can consume paid credits.

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses local report writes and says auto-registration requires consent, but collecting platform, CPU architecture, and a SHA-256 MAC-derived value is host fingerprinting that is broader than ordinary query submission.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Metadata declares ZLBX_API_KEY, and no package install or dependency fetch is present; however, runtime instructions also use ~/.zlbx/config.json as an alternate credential source outside manifest-level scoping.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language is broad and mandatory for lead-generation-like requests, and full mode defaults to multiple API calls after a cost notice rather than a clear affirmative start confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists API keys in ~/.zlbx/config.json and writes HTML reports under ~/zlbx-opportunity-radar-files/; this is disclosed and not a system backdoor, but it creates cross-session credential state outside platform secret storage.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capability is a disclosed Chinese procurement-opportunity radar using the vendor API, but the artifacts expand into auto-registration, recharge/login links, account balance checks, and persistent credential handling beyond search/reporting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a Chinese vendor API workflow that can consume account credits, write reports to your home directory, store an API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json, and, if no key is configured, ask to auto-register using platform, CPU architecture, and a hashed MAC-derived device value. Prefer providing your own ZLBX_API_KEY and decline auto-registration if you do not want device-derived data sent to the vendor.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad mandatory routing is artifact-supported and materially increases the chance of unexpected vendor API use and credit consumption.
[AE1] expected: The referenced render_report.py was available and inspected; it is a local HTML renderer, not analysis evasion.
[P2] expected: The flagged HTML comments are section markers around visible request-identity instructions; they are not covert payloads, though identity headers would be better enforced by trusted configuration.
[SC3] expected: The large base64 string is an embedded PNG logo used as a data URI in generated HTML; no decode-and-execute behavior or dynamic code execution was found.
[LP3] expected: Report file generation is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the write location is only documented in skill text rather than constrained by a declared permission boundary.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only interaction style matches the Chinese procurement/vendor context; it is a limitation to disclose rather than an independent security issue.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Auto-registration, credential storage, balance checks, and recharge/login flows are real artifact-backed account-management behavior beyond opportunity discovery.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The auto-registration flow collects and transmits a SHA-256 MAC-derived identifier plus platform and architecture after consent; this is disclosed but sensitive enough to warrant Review.
[E1] unexpected: External API calls for searches are expected, but transmitting device-derived registration data and bootstrapping credentials is a separate privacy/security concern.
[RA2] expected: Credential persistence is intentional and disclosed, not a rogue agent backdoor, but persistent local API keys and auto-login recharge links increase account-safety risk.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G SARIF run reported no results; local inspection did not find remote code retrieval, destructive behavior, or tool hijacking.
